transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, um, I’m here because... it's about work. Dispatch and compliance, they've been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And making these little comments on the radio. Which, actually, the radio in my cab has been acting up lately, it has this high-pitched hum. My brother tried to teach me about radio frequencies once when we were fixing up this old stereo my grandmother left us. She had all these beautiful antique things in her house... all this dark wood furniture that always smelled like lemon polish. You just don't see furniture like that anymore, everything you buy now is just cheap particle board, you know? It all breaks in a year. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the tracking. People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight, just them doing their jobs. But I can tell. I know certain drivers are reporting on me. They're definitely reporting on me to dispatch. Do you like antique furniture? I just think it has so much more character than the new stuff.
Do you believe that your coworkers or employers are intentionally trying to harm or monitor you in some way?

Well, yeah, they are definitely monitoring me. Intentionally. Like, even when people tell me it's just normal oversight for dispatch and compliance to watch the computer system, I know it's not. They track every single route change I make. And the other drivers are definitely reporting on me, I can hear them making those little comments on the radio about my location. 

Which, speaking of the radio, it's wired into the main cab battery, and my brother—he's the one who knows about frequencies—he said that vehicle batteries nowadays drain so fast because of all the extra electronics. We took a road trip once down to Florida and the alternator died right in the middle of Georgia. It was so hot, just that miserable, sticky humid heat, you know? We had to sit at this tiny roadside diner for six hours waiting for a tow, just eating peach cobbler. The cobbler was actually amazing, they used fresh peaches. I really think fresh fruit makes all the difference in baking. Canned peaches just get so mushy and weirdly sweet. Do you bake at all? 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the monitoring. Yeah, so dispatch. They're definitely tracking my routes on the computer. It's not just normal oversight, no matter what anyone says.
Do you ever hear sounds or voices that others don’t seem to hear?

Voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. Just normal sounds. I mean, my truck cab gets pretty loud, especially when I'm idling at the loading dock. It's a Peterbilt, and the diesel engine has this really heavy rumble that kind of rattles your teeth if you lean against the door. My uncle actually used to drive a Peterbilt back in the nineties. He used to take his dog with him on all his runs, this massive Golden Retriever named Buster. 

Buster shed everywhere, just huge clumps of blonde hair all over the seats. It's so hard to get dog hair out of upholstery, you know? You have to use one of those rubber squeegee things, because regular vacuums just don't cut it. I saw this infomercial the other night for a special pet hair vacuum, but those infomercials always make things look so much easier than they really are. They always have people struggling in black-and-white to use a normal broom, acting like they've never held one before in their entire lives. Do you ever watch late-night TV? It's mostly just those weird ads now... 

But, um... wait. Did you ask about my uncle? Or the truck? Oh, right, voices. No, I don't hear voices or anything. Just the normal noises around me.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by outside forces, or that certain things people say or do have a special meaning that's directed at you?

Controlled? No, no, nobody is putting thoughts in my head or anything like that. I mean, my thoughts are my own. It's just the dispatch system tracking me, which is annoying enough. We had to upgrade the software on those onboard computers last month, and it was a total disaster. The whole system was down for like two days, and they had us logging everything on paper. I actually didn't mind the paper logs, honestly. There's something satisfying about writing things down with a good pen. 

I have this one pen, it's a pilot G2, the blue ink one, and it just glides so perfectly. I always buy them in bulk from office supply stores because if you buy them at the gas station they're always dried out. Gas station stationery sections are the worst. It's always just dusty spiral notebooks and those cheap clicky pens that break in half if you press too hard. Have you ever noticed how everything at a gas station is covered in that thin layer of dust? Even the little powdered donuts. Though I guess that's just powdered sugar. 

But, um... what did you ask me? Something about the computers? Oh, right, thoughts being controlled. No, no, I don't feel like that at all. And people aren't sending me secret messages or anything. It's just the regular tracking stuff I told you about.
Do you ever feel like things people say or do in general—like things on the radio, TV, or in conversation—are meant specifically for you, even if they don’t seem to be?

Meant specifically for me? Like, on the TV or radio? No, not really. I mean, the guys on the CB radio are definitely talking about me, like I said, but that's just regular talking. The actual radio stations, like the music ones, they just play the same songs over and over. I listen to the classic rock station mostly, because the pop stations play way too many commercials. 

It feels like every three songs there's a block of ads for car dealerships. And those car dealership commercials are always so loud, they have that guy yelling about "crazy weekend sales events" with the echoing voice effect. It's so obnoxious. My dad actually bought a truck from one of those places once, a used Chevy Silverado. It was this awful bright red color, like a fire engine. He loved it, though. He used to spend every Sunday morning waxing it in the driveway. He had this special carnauba wax that smelled like coconuts. It always made the whole garage smell like a tropical vacation, which was weird because we lived in Ohio and it was usually snowing. Have you ever been to Ohio? The winters are just brutal, the gray skies just kind of press down on you for months...

Wait, sorry... what were we talking about? Oh, the radio and TV. Yeah, no, I don't think the people on TV or the DJs are talking to me or anything. It's just normal broadcasting.

Outside of work and the radio, do you ever feel like things happening around you—like things people say or do in public, or events you see—have a hidden or special meaning that’s directed at you personally?

Hidden meanings? Like in public? No, I don't really pay attention to people in public like that. I usually just keep my head down when I'm out, especially at the grocery store. I go to this big supermarket near my apartment, but I always try to go late at night when it's empty. The fluorescent lights in there are so bright, they kind of give me a headache if I stay too long. 

They recently remodeled the produce section, too, and they moved all the apples. It took me like twenty minutes just to find the Granny Smiths last week. I always buy Granny Smiths because they're the best for baking. My grandmother taught me how to make this incredible apple crisp when I was a kid. She had this old cast-iron skillet that she used for everything, and it was seasoned perfectly. You can't wash cast iron with soap, you know, you just have to wipe it out and oil it. Some people get so grossed out by that, but it really makes the food taste better. She used to fry bacon in it on Sunday mornings, and the smell would wake the whole house up. Bacon is so expensive now, though. I saw a pack at the store the other day and it was almost ten dollars. Can you believe that? Ten dollars for bacon... 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Something about the grocery store? Oh, right, hidden meanings in public. No, no, I don't see any special meanings or anything. Just people doing their own thing, shopping and stuff.
Do you ever feel like you're involved in something bigger—like part of a special mission or important event that most people don't know about?

A special mission? No, I'm just a driver. I mean, my job is important, but it's not a secret mission or anything like that. I just haul freight. Mostly auto parts lately, actually. They've had me doing this route between Detroit and Toledo, and the traffic on I-75 is just a nightmare. There's this one stretch where they've been doing construction for what feels like three years. They have those concrete barriers up, and it gets so narrow, you feel like you're going to scrape the side of your rig against them. 

I saw a guy in a little Honda Civic totally side-swipe one of those barriers last week. Sparks went everywhere. He just kept driving, though. Probably didn't have insurance. Car insurance is such a scam anyway. I pay so much every month, and when someone backed into my personal car last year—a little Hyundai Elantra—the insurance company tried to tell me it was my fault because I was parked too close to the line. I wasn't even in the car! I was inside getting a coffee. I always get the medium roast with two creams, no sugar. Sugar in coffee just ruins the taste of the beans, you know? My sister puts so much flavored syrup in hers it barely looks like coffee anymore. It's like a milkshake. She works at a dental office, too, which is ironic considering how much sugar she drinks...

Wait, sorry... what were you saying? A special mission? No, no, nothing like that. Just regular work, driving the truck, dealing with the traffic. Nothing special.
Outside of work-related tracking or monitoring, have you ever felt that others are spying on you, following you, or acting against you as part of some kind of conspiracy?

Spying on me? Or like a conspiracy? Outside of work? No, not really. I mean, my landlord is pretty nosy, but that's just because he lives in the unit downstairs. He's always out on his porch when I come home, smoking those cheap cigars. They smell absolutely awful, like burning tires or something. 

He's got this little dog, too, a pug I think. It breathes so loudly, it always sounds like it's struggling. Pugs have so many health problems, you know? It's kind of sad that people keep breeding them just because they look cute. My cousin used to breed Golden Retrievers, which is totally different. They're such great family dogs. She had this one named Buster who would carry a tennis ball in his mouth everywhere he went. Even when he was sleeping, he'd have it tucked right under his chin. He lived to be, like, fourteen, which is really old for a big dog. They had to bury him out in the backyard under this big oak tree. Oak trees drop so many acorns in the fall, it's a nightmare if you have to mow the lawn. The mower blades just shoot them out like little projectiles. You could really take an eye out if you aren't careful. That's why I always wear safety glasses when I do yard work. Well, I used to, when I had a yard. Now I just have a little balcony, and I can't even keep a fern alive on it...

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about my landlord? Oh, conspiracies. No, I don't think anyone is spying on me or anything. Just the normal nosy neighbors, but no conspiracies.
Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t agree with — something that made you feel very different from the people around you?

Believed something strongly that others didn't agree with? Like an opinion or something? I don't know, I guess I have opinions, but nothing crazy. I try not to argue with people, honestly. It's just exhausting. Like my friend Sarah, she is always trying to argue with me about politics. She watches the news constantly, like, all day long. I tell her it's bad for her blood pressure. 

High blood pressure runs in my family, actually. My dad had to go on medication for it when he was only forty-five. He hated taking pills, though. He used to hide them in his pocket and pretend he swallowed them, like a little kid. My mom would find them in the laundry all the time. The washing machine would just disintegrate them into this chalky white paste on all his dark jeans. Denim is so hard to get stains out of, too. I read once that you're not actually supposed to wash your jeans very often, you're just supposed to put them in the freezer to kill the bacteria. I tried that once, but it just made my freezer smell like outside, and then my frozen pizzas tasted weird. I love those little personal pizzas, the ones with the tiny square pepperonis. They always burn the roof of my mouth because I can never wait for them to cool down. It's like the cheese turns into lava. The roof of your mouth takes forever to heal, too, it just stays raw for days...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about Sarah? Or opinions? No, I don't really have any strong beliefs that make me feel different or anything. I just try to keep to myself mostly.
Outside of your experiences at work, have you ever felt that things happening around you—like things people say or do—were secretly about you or meant to target you in some way?

Secretly about me? Like people talking about me behind my back? I mean, sometimes I wonder if the girls at the terminal are gossiping, but that's just how people are, right? People love to talk. My aunt Susan is the worst for that. She literally calls my mom every Sunday night just to complain about her neighbors. She lives in this over-55 community in Florida, and you'd think it would be peaceful, but it's like high school down there. 

There's this whole drama about the community pool and who gets to use the good lounge chairs. They have these really nice ones with the thick cushions, but there are only six of them, so people go down at like 5:00 AM to put their towels on them to claim them. It's ridiculous. I don't even like swimming in public pools anyway. The chlorine dries out my skin so badly, and it makes my hair feel like straw. I have to use this special deep conditioner, the kind with argan oil in it. It smells amazing, kind of like vanilla and amber, but it's so expensive. I usually try to buy it when they have the buy-one-get-one-half-off sale at Ulta. Ulta is dangerous, though. You go in for one thing, and suddenly you've spent eighty dollars on lip gloss and face masks. I have this one clay mask that turns bright green when it dries, and it always scares the delivery guy if I open the door while I'm wearing it...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, people targeting me? No, I don't think so. Just regular gossip, maybe, but nothing secret or meant to target me. I don't really pay attention to that stuff anyway.

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about my landlord? Oh, conspiracies. No, I don't think anyone is spying on me or anything. Just the normal nosy neighbors, but no conspiracies.

patient.answer:
Believed something strongly that others didn't agree with? Like an opinion or something? I don't know, I guess I have opinions, but nothing crazy. I try not to argue with people, honestly. It's just exhausting. Like my friend Sarah, she is always trying to argue with me about politics. She watches the news constantly, like, all day long. I tell her it's bad for her blood pressure. 

High blood pressure runs in my family, actually. My dad had to go on medication for it when he was only forty-five. He hated taking pills, though. He used to hide them in his pocket and pretend he swallowed them, like a little kid. My mom would find them in the laundry all the time. The washing machine would just disintegrate them into this chalky white paste on all his dark jeans. Denim is so hard to get stains out of, too. I read once that you're not actually supposed to wash your jeans very often, you're just supposed to put them in the freezer to kill the bacteria. I tried that once, but it just made my freezer smell like outside, and then my frozen pizzas tasted weird. I love those little personal pizzas, the ones with the tiny square pepperonis. They always burn the roof of my mouth because I can never wait for them to cool down. It's like the cheese turns into lava. The roof of your mouth takes forever to heal, too, it just stays raw for days...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about Sarah? Or opinions? No, I don't really have any strong beliefs that make me feel different or anything. I just try to keep to myself mostly.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has ever experienced delusions of reference or persecution outside of the work context, which could indicate a more generalized delusional disorder or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Outside of your experiences at work, have you ever felt that things happening around you—like things people say or do—were secretly about you or meant to target you in some way?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about ideas of reference (believing unrelated events or actions are secretly about or targeting the patient) outside of work. patient.answer:
Secretly about me? Like people talking about me behind my back? I mean, sometimes I wonder if the girls at the terminal are gossiping, but that's just how people are, right? People love to talk. My aunt Susan is the worst for that. She literally calls my mom every Sunday night just to complain about her neighbors. She lives in this over-55 community in Florida, and you'd think it would be peaceful, but it's like high school down there. 

There's this whole drama about the community pool and who gets to use the good lounge chairs. They have these really nice ones with the thick cushions, but there are only six of them, so people go down at like 5:00 AM to put their towels on them to claim them. It's ridiculous. I don't even like swimming in public pools anyway. The chlorine dries out my skin so badly, and it makes my hair feel like straw. I have to use this special deep conditioner, the kind with argan oil in it. It smells amazing, kind of like vanilla and amber, but it's so expensive. I usually try to buy it when they have the buy-one-get-one-half-off sale at Ulta. Ulta is dangerous, though. You go in for one thing, and suddenly you've spent eighty dollars on lip gloss and face masks. I have this one clay mask that turns bright green when it dries, and it always scares the delivery guy if I open the door while I'm wearing it...

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, people targeting me? No, I don't think so. Just regular gossip, maybe, but nothing secret or meant to target me. I don't really pay attention to that stuff anyway.
